request.spec:
I think of age in whole weeks, not days. Age should now be the number of complete seven-day
weeks from onset to the anchor (drop any leftover days). If the onset is after the anchor the
age is negative, counted the same way toward zero, so an onset ten days after the anchor is
minus one week, not minus two.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for this implementation's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
I think of age in whole weeks, not days. Age should now be the number of complete seven-day
weeks from onset to the anchor (drop any leftover days). If the onset is after the anchor the
age is negative, counted the same way toward zero, so an onset ten days after the anchor is
minus one week, not minus two.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Age is now counted in complete weeks instead of days, and `bin/e2e` passes.

The fix is one line in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/people/Person.java:131`: age now uses `ChronoUnit.WEEKS.between(onset, anchor)` instead of counting days. This counts only complete seven-day weeks and rounds negative ages toward zero, so an onset ten days after the anchor gives −1, as you asked. Decay is still momentum minus age, so it uses the week value automatically.

Nothing else needed to change: the stored data, the test seed endpoints and the page's display code are the same as before. I also updated the comments in `Person.java` and in the front end's `people.ts` so they say weeks instead of days.
